citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
The facility did not perform adequate daily observations in order to timely observe and directly communicate to a
veterinarian a problem with a female Yorkie. Dog #012 was identified a few days ago by a family member to be limping on
the right front leg. It was not until the inspection today that the licensee noted the dog had gotten its right front leg through
the chain collar and the chain collar was embedded into the skin around the chest of the dog. The dog was reactive upon
the removal of the chain collar by the licensee. After removal of the collar, the licensee commented that the collar smelled
bad. Prior to removal of the chain collar the dog was observed by the inspector to be holding up the right front leg and not
wanting to put much weight onto it. This continued after the collar was removed.
Daily observations must be conducted on all animals to assess their health and well-being. If an issue is seen, direct and
frequent communication with the veterinarian is required so that timely and appropriate care can be given to the affected
animal. Correct by having Dog #012 be evaluated by a veterinarian by noon on Saturday, October 3, 2026.

The Record of Dogs on Hand was not available for review at the time of inspection. The licensee was not able to find this
paperwork. The Record of Dogs on Hand (APHIS 7005) is a required document that lists each dog at a regulated facility
and includes information required under §2.75(a)(1)(i-ix). Each dealer shall make, keep, and maintain records which fully
and correctly disclose that information for dogs purchased or otherwise acquired, owned, held, or otherwise in their
possession. Ensure by maintaining a complete Record of Dogs on Hand for all dogs at the facility. Correct by: October 16,
2026.

citations.desc: Cleaning, sanitization, housekeeping, and pest control.
citations.narrative:
The facility does not have an effective program in place for the control of rodents. There are rodent droppings in multiple
areas throughout the kennel, including on the floor of the building, on the countertop by medications, and within dog
enclosures. One empty rodent trap was seen. Pests such as rodents may serve as sources of infection, fleas, or injury to
the dogs in the kennel. Correct by ensuring an effective program for the control of rodent pests is established and
maintained so as to promote the health and well-being of the dogs. Correct by: October 16, 2026.

The facility is overdue for the regularly scheduled site visit by the Attending Veterinarian. Regularly scheduled visits, not
less than every 12 months, by the attending veterinarian to assess and ensure the adequacy of veterinary care and other
aspects of animal use and care is required by the Animal Welfare Act. Correct by November 1, 2026.

The facility is overdue on the complete physical examinations performed by the veterinarian yearly in adult dogs. These
examinations were last performed in 2024. Annual physical examinations help to ensure the physical condition of dogs for
breeding. Correct by ensuring a complete physical examination from head to tail is performed on adult dogs by the
veterinarian not less than once every 12 months. Correct by: Nov 1, 2026.

The facility is not following the Program of Vet Care (PVC) for vaccines and heartworm and fecal testing. The PVC
prescribes for rabies, distemper, and parvovirus vaccines to be given yearly in adult dogs. These vaccines were last
performed in 2024. The PVC prescribes for heartworm and fecal testing to be performed on 25% of the adult dogs
annually. These tests were also performed last in 2024.
Routine preventative care such as vaccines and heartworm and fecal testing are performed to help prevent contagious
and/or deadly diseases of dogs and for early detection of parasites. Following the PVC allows for adequate veterinary
care of the dogs.
Correct by ensuring the facility follows a schedule for routine vaccines (rabies, distemper, and parvovirus) and routine
heartworm and fecal testing, in accordance with the PVC. Correct by: Nov 1, 2026.

The facility is not following a preventative care schedule to ensure healthy and unmatted hair coats. Six of the adult dogs
had significant mats. One male Cavalier Spaniel had significant matting on the outer ear flaps of both ears. Five Yorkie
terriers had significant matting along the back and sides. The licensee reported they had not been groomed in
approximately a year. Matting of the hair coat may lead to skin problems and discomfort in the dogs. Correct by ensuring
a preventative care plan to ensure healthy and unmatted hair coats is followed, as per the PVC. Correct by: October 16,
2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the license.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
